how_to_read.heading: How to read a page
how_to_read.lead: Every page is one day and one recipe, and every page is laid out the same way, so you always know where to look.
items: The big number is today. The small line under it counts the days of the year, from 1 to 365.
That is the year. The dot is today, and the dark part is how far through you are. The four small pictures are winter, spring, summer, autumn and winter again.
What you are aiming for, more or less.
What to get out of the cupboard, then how long it takes: the total first, then how much of that is you and how much is the oven.
What to buy. Every recipe feeds four.
Salt, pepper, herbs and spices live in their own list, because you probably have them already. Amounts are in the method where they matter.
A handful of steps. Read them all once before you start.

introduction.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Nobody cuts out ultra processed food overnight. You try. You read a label in the supermarket, feel guilty, put it in the basket anyway and go home.

This book started with that guilt. Ritika brought it to us as a problem: she wanted to cook with fewer ultra processed things and more of what is in season, and she wanted it to be easy. We thought about apps, games and scoreboards. Then we made the least techy thing we could, a book that sits in the kitchen.

The idea is small on purpose. One recipe a day. Each one uses what is in season that week, a normal supermarket, a normal kitchen and not much of your attention. Do that for a year and you have cooked 365 real meals without once having to decide what real food is.
You will miss days. Everyone does. There is no catching up and no streak to protect. Open the book at today's date and cook that one.
rules: If an ingredient would baffle a grandparent's cupboard, it is not in here.
Everything is on the shelves of a big, ordinary one.
A pan, a tray, a knife. No gadgets.
If it is not growing or storing well this month, it waits.
Most of the time on the clock is the oven or the pan doing it for you.
made: Seasoned was built in a single day, live on Twitch, as day 16 of 40 for 40. The recipes were written with AI. Every one was then checked against the rules above and read by a second AI whose only job is to be picky. The pictures are painted by AI too.
We have not cooked all 365 ourselves yet. If one lets you down, tell us and we will fix it.

paragraphs: This book began as a problem posed by Ritika: ultra processed food guilt. Thank you to everyone on the 40 for 40 team and the Twitch viewers who helped shape the idea, the recipes and the name.

about.heading: About the authors
paragraphs: Benjamin Bourdin, Lawrence Kao and Samira Sohail make 40 for 40: forty apps in forty days, built live on Twitch from London with guests who have never built software before.
Seasoned is day 16. It is the only one of the forty you can put on a shelf.

paragraphs: Seasoned is the first book in the series. Tell us what you'd like next: 365 lunches, a daily dinner, and more.
